ESV.1: Now Adam knew Eve his wife, and she conceived and bore Cain, saying, “I have gotten  a man with the help of the LORD.”
ESV.2: And again, she bore his brother Abel. Now Abel was a keeper of sheep, and Cain a worker of the ground.
ESV.3: In the course of time Cain brought to the LORD an offering of the fruit of the ground,
ESV.4: and Abel also brought of the firstborn of his flock and of their fat portions. And the LORD had regard for Abel and his offering,
ESV.5: but for Cain and his offering he had no regard. So Cain was very angry, and his face fell.
ESV.6: The LORD said to Cain, “Why are you angry, and why has your face fallen?
ESV.7: If you do well, will you not be accepted?  And if you do not do well, sin is crouching at the door. Its desire is contrary to  you, but you must rule over it.”
ESV.8: Cain spoke to Abel his brother.  And when they were in the field, Cain rose up against his brother Abel and killed him.
ESV.9: Then the LORD said to Cain, “Where is Abel your brother?” He said, “I do not know; am I my brother's keeper?”
ESV.10: And the LORD said, “What have you done? The voice of your brother's blood is crying to me from the ground.
ESV.11: And now you are cursed from the ground, which has opened its mouth to receive your brother's blood from your hand.
ESV.12: When you work the ground, it shall no longer yield to you its strength. You shall be a fugitive and a wanderer on the earth.”
ESV.13: Cain said to the LORD, “My punishment is greater than I can bear.
ESV.14: Behold, you have driven me today away from the ground, and from your face I shall be hidden. I shall be a fugitive and a wanderer on the earth, and whoever finds me will kill me.”
ESV.15: Then the LORD said to him, “Not so! If anyone kills Cain, vengeance shall be taken on him sevenfold.” And the LORD put a mark on Cain, lest any who found him should attack him.
ESV.16: Then Cain went away from the presence of the LORD and settled in the land of Nod,  east of Eden.
ESV.17: Cain knew his wife, and she conceived and bore Enoch. When he built a city, he called the name of the city after the name of his son, Enoch.
ESV.18: To Enoch was born Irad, and Irad fathered Mehujael, and Mehujael fathered Methushael, and Methushael fathered Lamech.
ESV.19: And Lamech took two wives. The name of the one was Adah, and the name of the other Zillah.
ESV.20: Adah bore Jabal; he was the father of those who dwell in tents and have livestock.
ESV.21: His brother's name was Jubal; he was the father of all those who play the lyre and pipe.
ESV.22: Zillah also bore Tubal-cain; he was the forger of all instruments of bronze and iron. The sister of Tubal-cain was Naamah.
ESV.23: Lamech said to his wives: “Adah and Zillah, hear my voice; you wives of Lamech, listen to what I say: I have killed a man for wounding me, a young man for striking me.
ESV.24: If Cain's revenge is sevenfold, then Lamech's is seventy-sevenfold.”
ESV.25: And Adam knew his wife again, and she bore a son and called his name Seth, for she said, “God has appointed  for me another offspring instead of Abel, for Cain killed him.”
ESV.26: To Seth also a son was born, and he called his name Enosh. At that time people began to call upon the name of the LORD.

NASB.1: Now the man had relations with his wife Eve, and she conceived and gave birth to Cain, and she said, 'I have gotten a manchild with [the help of] the LORD.'
NASB.2: Again, she gave birth to his brother Abel. And Abel was a keeper of flocks, but Cain was a tiller of the ground.
NASB.3: So it came about in the course of time that Cain brought an offering to the LORD of the fruit of the ground.
NASB.4: Abel, on his part also brought of the firstlings of his flock and of their fat portions. And the LORD had regard for Abel and for his offering;
NASB.5: but for Cain and for his offering He had no regard. So Cain became very angry and his countenance fell.
NASB.6: Then the LORD said to Cain, 'Why are you angry? And why has your countenance fallen?
NASB.7: 'If you do well, will not [your countenance] be lifted up? And if you do not do well, sin is crouching at the door; and its desire is for you, but you must master it.'
NASB.8: Cain told Abel his brother. And it came about when they were in the field, that Cain rose up against Abel his brother and killed him.
NASB.9: Then the LORD said to Cain, 'Where is Abel your brother?' And he said, 'I do not know. Am I my brother's keeper?'
NASB.10: He said, 'What have you done? The voice of your brother's blood is crying to Me from the ground.
NASB.11: 'Now you are cursed from the ground, which has opened its mouth to receive your brother's blood from your hand.
NASB.12: 'When you cultivate the ground, it will no longer yield its strength to you; you will be a vagrant and a wanderer on the earth.'
NASB.13: Cain said to the LORD, 'My punishment is too great to bear!
NASB.14: 'Behold, You have driven me this day from the face of the ground; and from Your face I will be hidden, and I will be a vagrant and a wanderer on the earth, and whoever finds me will kill me.'
NASB.15: So the LORD said to him, 'Therefore whoever kills Cain, vengeance will be taken on him sevenfold.' And the LORD appointed a sign for Cain, so that no one finding him would slay him.
NASB.16: Then Cain went out from the presence of the LORD, and settled in the land of Nod, east of Eden.
NASB.17: Cain had relations with his wife and she conceived, and gave birth to Enoch; and he built a city, and called the name of the city Enoch, after the name of his son.
NASB.18: Now to Enoch was born Irad, and Irad became the father of Mehujael, and Mehujael became the father of Methushael, and Methushael became the father of Lamech.
NASB.19: Lamech took to himself two wives: the name of the one was Adah, and the name of the other, Zillah.
NASB.20: Adah gave birth to Jabal; he was the father of those who dwell in tents and [have] livestock.
NASB.21: His brother's name was Jubal; he was the father of all those who play the lyre and pipe.
NASB.22: As for Zillah, she also gave birth to Tubal-cain, the forger of all implements of bronze and iron; and the sister of Tubal-cain was Naamah.
NASB.23: Lamech said to his wives, 'Adah and Zillah, Listen to my voice, You wives of Lamech, Give heed to my speech, For I have killed a man for wounding me; And a boy for striking me;
NASB.24: If Cain is avenged sevenfold, Then Lamech seventy-sevenfold.'
NASB.25: Adam had relations with his wife again; and she gave birth to a son, and named him Seth, for, [she said], 'God has appointed me another offspring in place of Abel, for Cain killed him.'
NASB.26: To Seth, to him also a son was born; and he called his name Enosh. Then [men] began to call upon the name of the LORD.

NLT.1: Now Adam had sexual relations with his wife, Eve, and she became pregnant. When she gave birth to Cain, she said, “With the LORD’s help, I have produced a man!”
NLT.2: Later she gave birth to his brother and named him Abel. When they grew up, Abel became a shepherd, while Cain cultivated the ground.
NLT.3: When it was time for the harvest, Cain presented some of his crops as a gift to the LORD.
NLT.4: Abel also brought a gift — the best portions of the firstborn lambs from his flock. The LORD accepted Abel and his gift,
NLT.5: but he did not accept Cain and his gift. This made Cain very angry, and he looked dejected.
NLT.6: “Why are you so angry?” the LORD asked Cain. “Why do you look so dejected?
NLT.7: You will be accepted if you do what is right. But if you refuse to do what is right, then watch out! Sin is crouching at the door, eager to control you. But you must subdue it and be its master.”
NLT.8: One day Cain suggested to his brother, “Let’s go out into the fields.” And while they were in the field, Cain attacked his brother, Abel, and killed him.
NLT.9: Afterward the LORD asked Cain, “Where is your brother? Where is Abel?” “I don’t know,” Cain responded. “Am I my brother’s guardian?”
NLT.10: But the LORD said, “What have you done? Listen! Your brother’s blood cries out to me from the ground!
NLT.11: Now you are cursed and banished from the ground, which has swallowed your brother’s blood.
NLT.12: No longer will the ground yield good crops for you, no matter how hard you work! From now on you will be a homeless wanderer on the earth.”
NLT.13: Cain replied to the LORD, “My punishment is too great for me to bear!
NLT.14: You have banished me from the land and from your presence; you have made me a homeless wanderer. Anyone who finds me will kill me!”
NLT.15: The LORD replied, “No, for I will give a sevenfold punishment to anyone who kills you.” Then the LORD put a mark on Cain to warn anyone who might try to kill him.
NLT.16: So Cain left the LORD’s presence and settled in the land of Nod, east of Eden.
NLT.17: Cain had sexual relations with his wife, and she became pregnant and gave birth to Enoch. Then Cain founded a city, which he named Enoch, after his son.
NLT.18: Enoch had a son named Irad. Irad became the father of Mehujael. Mehujael became the father of Methushael. Methushael became the father of Lamech.
NLT.19: Lamech married two women. The first was named Adah, and the second was Zillah.
NLT.20: Adah gave birth to Jabal, who was the first of those who raise livestock and live in tents.
NLT.21: His brother’s name was Jubal, the first of all who play the harp and flute.
NLT.22: Lamech’s other wife, Zillah, gave birth to a son named Tubal-cain. He became an expert in forging tools of bronze and iron. Tubal-cain had a sister named Naamah.
NLT.23:
One day Lamech said to his wives, “Adah and Zillah, hear my voice;
listen to me, you wives of Lamech.
I have killed a man who attacked me,
a young man who wounded me.
NLT.24:
If someone who kills Cain is punished seven times,
then the one who kills me will be punished seventy-seven times!”
NLT.25: Adam had sexual relations with his wife again, and she gave birth to another son. She named him Seth, for she said, “God has granted me another son in place of Abel, whom Cain killed.”
NLT.26: When Seth grew up, he had a son and named him Enosh. At that time people first began to worship the LORD by name.

WEB.1: The man knew  Eve his wife. She conceived,  and gave birth to Cain, and said, “I have gotten a man with Yahweh’s help.”
WEB.2: Again she gave birth, to Cain’s brother Abel. Abel was a keeper of sheep, but Cain was a tiller of the ground.
WEB.3: As time passed, Cain brought an offering to Yahweh from the fruit of the ground.
WEB.4: Abel also brought some of the firstborn of his flock and of its fat. Yahweh respected Abel and his offering,
WEB.5: but he didn’t respect Cain and his offering. Cain was very angry, and the expression on his face fell.
WEB.6: Yahweh said to Cain, “Why are you angry? Why has the expression of your face fallen?
WEB.7: If you do well, won’t it be lifted up? If you don’t do well, sin crouches at the door. Its desire is for you, but you are to rule over it.”
WEB.8: Cain said to Abel, his brother, “Let’s go into the field.” While they were in the field, Cain rose up against Abel, his brother, and killed him.
WEB.9: Yahweh said to Cain, “Where is Abel, your brother?” He said, “I don’t know. Am I my brother’s keeper?”
WEB.10: Yahweh said, “What have you done? The voice of your brother’s blood cries to me from the ground.
WEB.11: Now you are cursed because of the ground, which has opened its mouth to receive your brother’s blood from your hand.
WEB.12: From now on, when you till the ground, it won’t yield its strength to you. You will be a fugitive and a wanderer in the earth.”
WEB.13: Cain said to Yahweh, “My punishment is greater than I can bear.
WEB.14: Behold, you have driven me out today from the surface of the ground. I will be hidden from your face, and I will be a fugitive and a wanderer in the earth. Whoever finds me will kill me.”
WEB.15: Yahweh said to him, “Therefore whoever slays Cain, vengeance will be taken on him sevenfold.” Yahweh appointed a sign for Cain, so that anyone finding him would not strike him.
WEB.16: Cain left Yahweh’s presence, and lived in the land of Nod, east of Eden.
WEB.17: Cain knew his wife. She conceived, and gave birth to Enoch. He built a city, and called the name of the city, after the name of his son, Enoch.
WEB.18: To Enoch was born Irad. Irad became the father of Mehujael. Mehujael became the father of Methushael. Methushael became the father of Lamech.
WEB.19: Lamech took two wives: the name of the first one was Adah, and the name of the second one was Zillah.
WEB.20: Adah gave birth to Jabal, who was the father of those who dwell in tents and have livestock.
WEB.21: His brother’s name was Jubal, who was the father of all who handle the harp and pipe.

AMP.1: Now the man Adam knew Eve as his wife, and she conceived and gave birth to Cain, and she said, "I have obtained a man (baby boy, son) with the help of the LORD."
AMP.2: And [later] she gave birth to his brother Abel. Now Abel kept the flocks [of sheep and goats], but Cain cultivated the ground.
AMP.3: And in the course of time Cain brought to the LORD an offering of the fruit of the ground.
AMP.4: But Abel brought [an offering of] the [finest] firstborn of his flock and the fat portions. And the LORD had respect (regard) for Abel and for his offering;
AMP.5: but for Cain and his offering He had no respect. So Cain became extremely angry (indignant), and he looked annoyed and hostile.
AMP.6: And the LORD said to Cain, "Why are you so angry? And why do you look annoyed?
AMP.7: If you do well [believing Me and doing what is acceptable and pleasing to Me], will you not be accepted? And if you do not do well [but ignore My instruction], sin crouches at your door; its desire is for you [to overpower you], but you must master it."
AMP.8: Cain talked with Abel his brother [about what God had said]. And when they were [alone, working] in the field, Cain attacked Abel his brother and killed him.
AMP.9: Then the LORD said to Cain, "Where is Abel your brother?" And he [lied and] said, "I do not know. Am I my brother's keeper?"
AMP.10: The LORD said, "What have you done? The voice of your brother's [innocent] blood is crying out to Me from the ground [for justice].
AMP.11: And now you are cursed from the ground, which has opened its mouth to receive your brother's [shed] blood from your hand.
AMP.12: When you cultivate the ground, it shall no longer yield its strength [it will resist producing good crops] for you; you shall be a fugitive and a vagabond [roaming aimlessly] on the earth [in perpetual exile without a home, a degraded outcast]."
AMP.13: Cain said to the LORD, "My punishment is greater than I can bear.
AMP.14: Behold, You have driven me out this day from the face of the land; and from Your face (presence) I will be hidden, and I will be a fugitive and an [aimless] vagabond on the earth, and whoever finds me will kill me."
AMP.15: And the LORD said to him, " Therefore, whoever kills Cain, a sevenfold vengeance [that is, punishment seven times worse] shall be taken on him [by Me]." And the LORD set a [protective] mark (sign) on Cain, so that no one who found (met) him would kill him.
AMP.16: So Cain went away from the [manifested] presence of the LORD, and lived in the land of Nod [wandering in exile], east of Eden.
AMP.17: Cain knew his wife [one of Adam's descendants] and she conceived and gave birth to Enoch; and Cain built a city and named it Enoch, after the name of his son.
AMP.18: Now to Enoch was born Irad, and Irad became the father of Mehujael, and Mehujael became the father of Methushael, and Methushael became the father of Lamech.
AMP.19: And Lamech took for himself two wives; the name of the one was Adah, and the name of the other, Zillah.
AMP.20: Adah gave birth to Jabal; he became the father of those [nomadic herdsmen] who live in tents and have cattle and raise livestock.
AMP.21: His brother's name was Jubal; he became the father of all those [musicians] who play the lyre and flute.
AMP.22: Zillah gave birth to Tubal-cain, the smith (craftsman) and teacher of every artisan in instruments of bronze and iron. The sister of Tubal-cain was Naamah.
AMP.23:
Lamech said to his wives,
"Adah and Zillah,
Hear my voice;
You wives of Lamech,
Listen to what I say;
For I have killed a man [merely] for wounding me,
And a boy [only] for striking (bruising) me.
AMP.24:
"If Cain is avenged sevenfold [as the LORD said he would be],
Then Lamech [will be avenged] seventy-sevenfold."
AMP.25: Adam knew [Eve as] his wife again; and she gave birth to a son, and named him Seth, for [she said], "God has granted another child for me in place of Abel, because Cain killed him."
AMP.26: To Seth, also, a son was born, whom he named Enosh (mortal man, mankind). At that [same] time men began to call on the name of the LORD [in worship through prayer, praise, and thanksgiving].

CSB17.1: The man was intimate with his wife Eve, and she conceived and gave birth to Cain. She said, “I have had a male child with the LORD’s help.” <sup>[1]</sup>
CSB17.2: She also gave birth to his brother Abel. Now Abel became a shepherd of flocks, but Cain worked the ground.
CSB17.3: In the course of time Cain presented some of the land’s produce as an offering to the LORD. <sup>ⓖ</sup>
CSB17.4: And Abel also presented an offering — some of the firstborn of his flock and their fat portions. <sup>ⓗ</sup> The LORD had regard for Abel and his offering, <sup>ⓘ</sup>
CSB17.5: but he did not have regard for Cain and his offering. Cain was furious, and he looked despondent. <sup>[2]</sup>
CSB17.6: Then the LORD said to Cain, “Why are you furious? <sup>ⓙ</sup> And why do you look despondent? <sup>[3]</sup>
CSB17.7: If you do what is right, won’t you be accepted? But if you do not do what is right, sin is crouching at the door. Its desire is for you, but you must rule over it.” <sup>ⓚ</sup>
CSB17.8: Cain said to his brother Abel, “Let’s go out to the field.” <sup>[4]</sup> And while they were in the field, Cain attacked his brother Abel and killed him. <sup>ⓛ</sup>
CSB17.9: Then the LORD said to Cain, “Where is your brother Abel?” “I don’t know,” he replied. “Am I my brother’s guardian?”
CSB17.10: Then he said, “What have you done? Your brother’s blood cries out to me from the ground! <sup>ⓜ</sup>
CSB17.11: So now you are cursed, alienated from the ground that opened its mouth to receive your brother’s blood you have shed. <sup>[5]</sup>
CSB17.12: If you work the ground, it will never again give you its yield. You will be a restless wanderer on the earth.” <sup>ⓝ</sup>
CSB17.13: But Cain answered the LORD, “My punishment <sup>[6]</sup> is too great to bear!
CSB17.14: Since you are banishing me today from the face of the earth, and I must hide from your presence and become a restless wanderer on the earth, whoever finds me will kill me.” <sup>ⓐ</sup>
CSB17.15: Then the LORD replied to him, “In that case, <sup>[7]</sup> whoever kills Cain will suffer vengeance seven times over.” <sup>[8]</sup> And he placed a mark <sup>ⓑ</sup> on Cain so that whoever found him would not kill him.
CSB17.16: Then Cain went out from the LORD’s presence and lived in the land of Nod, east of Eden.
CSB17.17: Cain was intimate with his wife, and she conceived and gave birth to Enoch. Then Cain became the builder of a city, and he named the city Enoch after his son.
CSB17.18: Irad was born to Enoch, Irad fathered Mehujael, Mehujael fathered Methushael, and Methushael fathered Lamech.
CSB17.19: Lamech took two wives for himself, one named Adah and the other named Zillah.
CSB17.20: Adah bore Jabal; he was the father of the nomadic herdsmen. <sup>[9]</sup>
CSB17.21: His brother was named Jubal; he was the father of all who play the lyre and the flute.
CSB17.22: Zillah bore Tubal-cain, who made all kinds of bronze and iron tools. Tubal-cain’s sister was Naamah.
CSB17.23:

wives of Lamech, pay attention to my words.

a young man for striking me.
CSB17.24:
If Cain is to be avenged seven times over,
then for Lamech it will be seventy-seven times!
CSB17.25: Adam was intimate with his wife again, and she gave birth to a son and named him Seth, for she said, “God has given <sup>[10]</sup> me another child <sup>[11]</sup> in place of Abel, since Cain killed him.”

NET.1: Now the man had marital relations with his wife Eve, and she became pregnant and gave birth to Cain. Then she said, “I have created a man just as the LORD did!”
NET.2: Then she gave birth to his brother Abel. Abel took care of the flocks, while Cain cultivated the ground.
NET.3: At the designated time Cain brought some of the fruit of the ground for an offering to the LORD.
NET.4: But Abel brought some of the firstborn of his flock — even the fattest of them. And the LORD was pleased with Abel and his offering,
NET.5: but with Cain and his offering he was not pleased. So Cain became very angry, and his expression was downcast.
NET.6: Then the LORD said to Cain, “Why are you angry, and why is your expression downcast?
NET.7: Is it not true that if you do what is right, you will be fine? But if you do not do what is right, sin is crouching at the door. It desires to dominate you, but you must subdue it.”

NET.9: Then the LORD said to Cain, “Where is your brother Abel?” And he replied, “I don’t know! Am I my brother’s guardian?”
NET.10: But the LORD said, “What have you done? The voice of your brother’s blood is crying out to me from the ground!
NET.11: So now, you are banished from the ground, which has opened its mouth to receive your brother’s blood from your hand.
